add.name: Trumans' Pioneer Stud Farm

facade.photoSource: Mark's illustrated postcard, Trumans' Pioneer Stud Farm.

add.notes: Location per Mark Rauschert, Nov 2026. The 1918 Good Hope sheet shows this wedge, between the CB&Q Quincy main and the St. Louis branch, open of the farmhouses copied from that sheet. The footprint is an estimate from the illustrated postcard. The painted signs and flags are the postcard, shown from 1900 through 1940. From 1941 the barns stay and those signs and flags come off. Post-1940 appearance unknown; buildings kept per Mark (some still standing in 2026); signs removed as unverified. survivesTo 2026 records that some of the buildings still stand. Which buildings is not recorded, so the group stays when later years are added. No year after 1970 is in the model. The postcard spelling is Trumans' Pioneer Stud Farm.

update.notes: photo from Mark, 590 E Main St, 2010. The East Main front is the cream facade in that photograph: red pilasters between the upper windows, red trim, BALL BROS in the pediment, and CARRIAGE on the right bay. The letters after CARRIAGE were not read. The pale curved roof behind that bay is the arch in the photograph. The 1907 biography says the main building then standing, 60 by 100 feet on Main Street, was erected in 1895. That is the date used. The photograph does not date the front, so showing it from the 1900 stop is an estimate. From that stop this front sits immediately south of the brick corner building. The 1880 and 1890 stops keep the 1880s false front on the earlier footprint. The hose tower stays on the 500 block.

update.notes: photo from Mark, 2010. North end of the 590 East Main block, the brick corner immediately north of the cream Ball Bros. front. The upper floor has round-arched windows. White circles between the window groups read M, C, and P. Those letters are not a name; no source found here says what they stand for. A red ball sits on the parapet. The ground floor is plate glass, with a white canopy on curved brackets. The building runs long down Gridley. The arched window beside the cream front in the other 2010 photograph is this same wall. No Sanborn label read for this pass names the block, so the date is an estimate and the front is drawn from the 1900 stop. The 1880 and 1890 stops keep the earlier Gridley brick. The stand-in Grocery and Boots doors that stood on this ground come off from 1900.

update.notes: The Hurst corner of the 400 block of East Main, Crafford side, block 59. Mark's view looking north, and the postcard taken from the 300 block, both show this corner as a two-story red brick bank. The signs read BANK OF BUSHNELL and DENTIST. A 1900 paving petition names the Bank of Bushnell as the end of an East Main stretch, and does not give the lot. No Sanborn label for this bank was read. The corner is the one across Hurst from the 300 block. The partial grocery word farther down the block is not copied as a firm name. photo from Mark, E Main 400 block south end, 2010, shows six tall upstairs windows under cream hoods, and a cornice with dentils, brackets, and a central pediment and finial. Those upper details are drawn here. The brick stays red, which is what the earlier photograph shows. The cream paint, the filled panels, and the ground-floor sign are the 2010 photograph and are not drawn in this year.

facade.photoSource: Mark's postcard, East Main St., Bushnell, Illinois, from the 300 block looking north.

update.notes: August 1893 Sanborn, sheet 2, the Hurst corner room of the brick block on the 300 block of East Main, block 72. Mark's postcard shows an ornate two-story brick with a corner bay and a projecting sign, BILLIARD HALL and LUNCH ROOM. Those are sign words, not an owner's name. The May 1898 sheet reads the corner room as Photo and a room further west as lunch, so which room carried the sign is an estimate. The 1893 sheet called this corner a market.

update.name: The Democrat
update.notes: The readable cornice sign in Mark's about-1900 view looking south on West Main. The McDonough Democrat began in 1884. A 1908 paving note sends a route east on Hail to the Democrat office, which puts the office at Hail and West Main, the near end of this view. The exact bay is an estimate. The photograph is not used to call any other door a newspaper.

update.name: Grocery
update.notes: Mark's view north on the 400 block of East Main shows a sign ending in GROCERY. The letters before it were not legible, so they are not used. This is the generic word only, on an existing stand-in past the pediment.
